Le **hangeul (한글)** a été créé en 1443 p: **Hangeul (한글)** was created in 1443 by King **Sejong the Great** so that all the people could read and write. It is an alphabet (not ideograms like Chinese): each letter represents a sound.
Il compte **24 lettres de base** (14 con: It has **24 basic letters** (14 consonants + 10 vowels), plus compound letters. The letters are grouped into **syllable blocks**: 한 = ㅎ + ㅏ + ㄴ.
Le 9 octobre est le « Jour du Hangeul »: 9 October is “Hangeul Day” (한글날), a public holiday in South Korea.
Les voyelles sont construites à partir d: Vowels are built from three elements: heaven (·), earth (ㅡ) and man (ㅣ). A vowel is **never written alone**: at the start of a syllable it is preceded by the silent consonant **ㅇ**.

**Verticales** (ㅏ ㅓ ㅣ ㅐ ㅔ) : la consonne: **Vertical** (ㅏ ㅓ ㅣ ㅐ ㅔ): the consonant goes **on the left** → 아, 어, 이.
**Horizontales** (ㅗ ㅜ ㅡ) : la consonne s: **Horizontal** (ㅗ ㅜ ㅡ): the consonant goes **on top** → 오, 우, 으.

Les consonnes de base imitent la positio: The basic consonants imitate the position of the tongue or lips: **ㄱ** shows the tongue touching the back of the palate, **ㄴ** the tongue against the teeth, **ㅁ** the closed mouth, **ㅅ** a tooth, **ㅇ** the throat.
ㄱ, ㄷ, ㅂ, ㅈ sont **légèrement sourdes** e: ㄱ, ㄷ, ㅂ, ㅈ are **slightly voiceless** at the start of a word (between g/k, d/t, b/p, j/ch) and become **voiced** between two vowels. So 고기 (meat) is pronounced almost “ko-gi”.
